intervals.note: True formation date not sourced (the collaboration certainly predates the Gran Sasso run under Carlo Rubbia's leadership); start is a lower bound taken from the May 2010 start of T600 operation at LNGS, the earliest dated collaboration activity found. The collaboration continues to operate the detector at Fermilab.
intervals.quote: was smoothly and safely operated from May 2010 to June 2013

name: ICARUS Collaboration
notes: Institution-level membership rows are owned by the membership-lead workstream and are not written here.
Leadership is left empty: person records are owned by another workstream. The ICARUS About page credits "the leadership of Nobel laureate Carlo Rubbia" for the Gran Sasso era (2010-2013).

summary.plain: The international team, originally led by Nobel laureate Carlo Rubbia, that built the ICARUS liquid-argon detector, ran it in Italy, rebuilt it at CERN, and now runs it at Fermilab.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating the ICARUS-T600 LArTPC: Gran Sasso (LNGS) 2010-2013 under Carlo Rubbia's leadership, CERN refurbishment 2014-2017, and Fermilab SBN far-detector operation since 2021.
